name: record-item-type
body: A list field's single item descriptor may declare an inline record: `item: {type: record, fields: [...]}`. A record's `fields:` uses exactly the same descriptors as a template's top-level fields — name, type, rules and description — so a record's field may be a list whose item is a record (records nest through a list's item descriptor), and every field and item descriptor may be `nullable` (nullable-fields). A record value is a YAML mapping validated recursively against its `fields:`; a type, required, unknown-key or rule violation is reported with its full path, for example `items › [2] › value: required — add a value: value`. `kalide templates <name>` prints a record field's shape, including its nested fields (cli-templates-show). In layouts a record's fields reach the execution context exactly like a template's top-level fields: its `text` fields arrive pre-rendered as safe HTML and its other fields as typed values (template-language, template-context).
